ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show fee; no refund, no account action. Advise the rider that the fee stands because the driver arrived, waited past the free-wait threshold, and attempted contact before cancelling.
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled the trip (F4), so the case runs under NS-0 as a driver-cancelled-for-no-show matter, assessed under NS-1 / NS-2 [NS-0]. The rider's complaint that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" does not disturb the fee if NS-1's conditions held [F4].

All four NS-1 conditions are satisfied on the record [NS-1]. (i) Arrival: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:21:55, 40 m from the pickup point, with a closest approach of 38 m — well within 200 m [F7][F1]. (ii) Wait: he then remained continuously at the pickup for 6 min 0 s (360 s) before cancelling at 18:27:55, exceeding the 5-minute free wait (300 s) counted from arrival [F7][F6]. (iii) Contact: before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 18:22:25, "At the pickup now, grey Kia Niro") and made 1 in-app call (18:23:25, not answered) [F5][F10][F13]. (iv) Presence: the GPS shows him stationary at 40 m from the pickup for the whole 18:21:55–18:27:55 window, so continuous presence is proven [F3]. There is no GPS gap of the kind that would send this to a person [F3][F7].

On NS-0's question — why he cancelled — the driver's own words are the test. Chat #2 at 18:27 reads "No reply from you, I need to go already, cancelling," and his statement says he waited more than 5 minutes with no rider [F11][F14]. Those are the rider's absence as the reason, not car trouble, a personal matter, another job, or a refusal of the trip; the app reason field was left empty, and an unpicked field is not a reason of his own [F4]. The element is therefore met and NS-1 holds, so the $5.00 fee on record stands [F8][NS-1]. No NS-1 condition failed, so NS-2's refund-and-flag branch is not triggered, and there are no prior no-shows in 30 days, so NS-9's flag does not apply [F8][F18][NS-2][NS-9]. The dispute concerns the flat $5.00 fee, fixed by NS-1 / NS-2; no route, surge, or traffic analysis bears on it (no deviation, surge 1.0×, no incidents) [F9][F16].

No refund or waiver is owed: the fee is the amount on record ($5.00) and is upheld [F8]. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel, zero contact, $5.00 upheld) is aligned in outcome; here, contact was made, which only strengthens the finding [NS-1]. Both briefs requested no_action, consistent with this result.

element_findings.reason: The driver's own words give the rider's absence as the reason for cancelling: "No reply from you, I need to go already, cancelling" [F11] and his statement that he waited over 5 minutes with no rider [F14]. Nothing names car trouble, a personal/family matter, another job or a refusal [F4]. His words therefore fall under NS-1, not NS-3 [NS-0].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's implied claim that the fee was charged "for nothing" fails: all four NS-1 conditions held — arrival within 200 m [F7][F1], a 360 s wait from arrival exceeding the 5-minute threshold [F7][F6], 2 messages and 1 call before cancelling [F5][F10][F13], and continuous presence at the pickup [F3]. NS-1 upholds the $5.00 fee [F8][NS-1].

The driver's request for no_action is correct in outcome and is granted, but it is not a separate claim requiring relief: the fee stands because NS-1's conditions are met on the record [F7][F5][F3][NS-1], and the unpicked app reason together with his chat and statement shows the rider's absence, not a reason of his own [F4][F11][F14][NS-0].
